The input structure is supplied in a nonstandard rhombohedral-like cell with all three lattice parameters equal to 6.80614309 Å and interaxial angles α = β = 109.19207959°, γ = 110.03095687°. This input cell contains 14 atoms with the declared composition Sr₂Ni₈Sn₄. The underlying symmetry is the tetragonal space group I4/mcm, space-group number 140, with Hall symbol “−I 4 2c.” Fractional coordinates are used throughout, and the supplied relation between the original input fractional coordinates q_input and the standard I4/mcm fractional coordinates q_standard is q_standard = P q_input + s. The transformation matrix P has rows (0.5000000000000001, −0.5, 0.5), (−0.5, 0.5000000000000001, 0.5), and (−0.5, −0.5, 0.5), while the origin shift s is (0.0, 0.0, 0.5). Thus the original nonstandard cell can be recovered from the conventional description only by applying this exact matrix and shift.

In the standard I4/mcm frame, the strontium sublattice occupies the fourfold Wyckoff orbit 4a, with representative fractional coordinate (0, 0, 1/4), written in the coordinate relation as “0, 0, 1/4.” This orbit has multiplicity 4 and no free positional parameters. Nickel occupies a single sixteenfold general-position-type orbit, 16l, with representative coordinate approximately (0.1362345, 0.6362345, 0.3377305). Its coordinate relation is “x, x+1/2, z,” with independent parameters x = 0.13623449999999998 and z = 0.33773049999999993; the second coordinate is therefore x + 1/2 = 0.6362345. Tin occupies the eightfold orbit 8h, represented by approximately (0.159755, 0.659755, 0). Its relation is “x, x+1/2, 0,” with the single independent parameter x = 0.15975499999999998, giving the paired coordinate x + 1/2 = 0.659755 and fixing the third coordinate at zero.

The three independent sublattices therefore consist of one Sr orbit on 4a, one Ni orbit on 16l, and one Sn orbit on 8h. Their multiplicities sum to 4 + 16 + 8 = 28 atoms in the conventional I-centered tetragonal cell, whereas the supplied nonstandard input cell contains 14 atoms, consistent with the stated input composition Sr₂Ni₈Sn₄. The body-centered tetragonal symmetry and the listed Wyckoff relations generate the full three-dimensional periodic arrangement from these three independent representative positions.

The input coordinates were rounded to six decimal places before correction. Two very small precision corrections are required to preserve the real input geometry rather than forcing it onto an exactly idealized coordinate value. One Sn atom at the pre-correction input fractional position (0.340245, 0.840245, 0.18049) is displaced by (0.0, 0.0, −1.000000000001 × 10⁻⁶), so only its third coordinate is lowered by about one part in 10⁶. A second Sn atom at the pre-correction input fractional position (0.659755, 0.159755, 0.81951) is displaced by (0.0, 0.0, +1.0000000000287557 × 10⁻⁶), raising only its third coordinate by the same order of magnitude. These corrections are explicit departures from the rounded input values and must be retained when reconstructing the supplied cell.
